title: Lookahead and lookbehind
explanation:
A **lookaround** checks what comes before or after the current position **without including it in the match**. Like `^` and `\b`, it is a zero-width assertion:

| Syntax | Matches `x` only if … |
|---|---|
| `x(?=y)` | followed by `y` (lookahead) |
| `x(?!y)` | **not** followed by `y` (negative lookahead) |
| `(?<=y)x` | preceded by `y` (lookbehind) |
| `(?<!y)x` | **not** preceded by `y` (negative lookbehind) |

```js
console.log("Jack Sprat".match(/Jack(?= Sprat)/)[0]);   // "Jack" -- " Sprat" is checked, not captured
console.log("3.141".match(/\d+(?!\.)/)[0]);             // "141"  -- "3" is followed by a dot
console.log("cost: -7 or 7".match(/(?<!-)\b\d+/)[0]);   // "7"    -- skips the negative number
```

Two patterns come up constantly. **Context without consuming** — grab a number only when a unit follows, or only after a currency sign. And **several independent conditions on the same text** — a lookahead placed right after `^` peeks at the whole string, and several of them can be stacked: `^(?=.*a)(?=.*b)` requires both an `a` and a `b`, in any order.
keyIdeas: Lookarounds test context but add nothing to the match.
Stack lookaheads after `^` to require several conditions in any order.

workedExample.problem: Check a password policy: at least 8 characters, containing at least one digit **and** at least one uppercase letter, in any order. `"Secret42x"` passes; `"secret42x"`, `"SecretXYZ"`, and `"Ab1"` fail.
steps: The length rule is ordinary matching: `^.{8,}$`.
"Contains a digit somewhere" is a lookahead at the start: `(?=.*\d)`. It peeks at the string without moving the position.
Add a second, independent lookahead for an uppercase letter: `(?=.*[A-Z])`.
Combine: `^(?=.*\d)(?=.*[A-Z]).{8,}$` — both lookaheads run from position 0, then `.{8,}$` checks the length.
workedExample.answer: `/^(?=.*\d)(?=.*[A-Z]).{8,}$/` — two lookaheads add the "contains" rules without consuming characters, and `.{8,}` enforces the length.

pitfalls: Expecting the lookahead text to appear in the match (it never does).
Writing `^(?!word)` when you mean "not exactly word" — it also rejects `"wordy"`; anchor with `$` inside the lookahead.
Putting `.*` lookaheads *after* consuming characters, so they only inspect the rest of the string.

citations.quote: Lookahead assertion: Matches "x" only if "x" is followed by "y".
Negative lookahead assertion: Matches "x" only if "x" is not followed by "y".
Lookbehind assertion: Matches "x" only if "x" is preceded by "y".
Negative lookbehind assertion: Matches "x" only if "x" is not preceded by "y".
However, neither "Sprat" nor "Frost" is part of the match results.
